decisions.decision: The preset picker is a map of the notation, and that is product truth
decisions.rationale: One worked example per InChI layer, chipped, leading the list in the order layers appear in a string. Recorded in PRODUCT.md with the reason: a layer with no example leaves an explanation card no user can reach, and a second example for a claimed layer breaks the one-to-one map. Asserted in presetLayerCoverage.test.ts against WASM-measured InChIs, not left to inspection.

decisions.decision: The 7.3MB first-load split was deferred, not skipped
decisions.rationale: It is the single biggest user-facing win left and the fix is known — move the lazy boundary from App down to KetcherPanel. Not shipped because it changes the mount path of a canvas PRODUCT.md calls load-bearing, there is no browser here to verify the editor still mounts exactly once, and an unexplained mount failure is already open on that same path. Making an unverifiable change there on top of an undiagnosed bug is how the bug becomes permanent.

decisions.decision: Accessibility left recorded as undecided, against the evidence of the code
decisions.rationale: The user chose this explicitly when asked. Worth knowing it is now an understatement: lib/keyboardProps.ts gives layer chunks role=button, tab stops, Enter/Space and arrow-key roving, every onMouseEnter has a paired onFocus, and colour is not the sole carrier of layer identity. Reported in the audit rather than repaired, because repairing drift as a side effect of a design task is forbidden.

decisions.decision: Maleic acid's InChI fixture kept after the molecule was removed from the picker
decisions.rationale: Fumaric and maleic are identical up to one sign character, which makes them the sharpest available check that the b layer's sign is parsed at all. Pulled out of ALL_FIXTURES and relabelled as parser coverage rather than deleted with the preset.

Verified rather than assumed during the audit: all 21 transition declarations across 7 files are background/color/opacity/box-shadow. There is no transform, translate or scale to suppress. A naive audit reports this as a defect and is wrong.

context_notes: Two process lessons worth carrying, both learned the hard way this session. First: I twice asserted the browser mount failure was not caused by my change, using a grep of my diff and a curl of the module graph — neither of which can distinguish innocent code from code that breaks at runtime. That needed a bisect or a test, and cost two rounds. Second: a guard is worthless until you try to break it. The first version of the tour-anchor test scanned all sources including HelpTour.tsx, so every assertion matched its own STEPS declaration and passed with the anchor deleted; I only found that by renaming the anchor and watching 27 tests stay green. Both failure modes look like diligence from the outside.
